item.title: With just a few primary elections to go, the competitive Senate map keeps shifting
item.description: For Democrats to take control of the U.S. Senate, they have to flip 4 seats currently held by Republicans. Republicans, meanwhile, are playing defense and pickup opportunities are harder to find.

item.title: Trump administration to announce rules for how states will share the Colorado River
item.description: This week the federal government is to release new rules for how much water each of the seven states that share the Colorado River will get. Effects on the ecosystem were largely left unconsidered.

item.title: Trump allies approve new rules that will weaken protections for historic sites
item.description: An advisory council stacked with President Trump's allies voted to relax a 60-year-old historic preservation law, paving the way for federal projects that could harm historic sites across the country.
item.content:encoded: An advisory council stacked with President Trump's allies voted to relax a 60-year-old historic preservation law, paving the way for federal projects that could harm historic sites across the country.

item.title: Meet the robots programmed by kids to speak their Indigenous languages
item.description: Many Native American languages are endangered. With the help of his mentor, a 12-year-old in Michigan hopes to help preserve his language through robotics.

item.title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break
item.description: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?

item.title: Wildfire alert in the Western U.S. reaches its highest level
item.description: Wildfires have now scorched four million acres of land in the U.S. Federal fire managers say all of the country's resources are currently deployed to major fires.

item.title: Biden ghostwriter tapes to be released
item.description: Former President Joe Biden is declining to appeal a court ruling that allows the Justice Department to publicize recordings of conversations between him and a writer collaborating on his memoir.

item.title: The bridge is up but the party is off: U.S. and Canada skip joint ribbon-cutting
item.description: The U.S. and Canada are opening a bridge between Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, without celebration as wildfires and tariffs increase tensions.
